title: Rethinking the Mechanisms of Alzheimer’s Disease - Nautilus
gist: Nautilus reports that the long-dominant view of Alzheimer's as primarily a toxic-protein disease is being challenged by findings pointing to a bloodstream/cerebral-vascular origin, and stresses that dementia is not only a memory disorder.

themes.theme: Vascular origin challenges the amyloid orthodoxy

insights.claim: Recent findings suggest Alzheimer's disease may originate in the bloodstream rather than in a buildup of toxic proteins, the cause researchers believed in for many years.
insights.so_what: A vascular-origin model would shift therapeutic value away from anti-amyloid programs toward cardiovascular and cerebral blood-flow interventions.
insights.quote: But recent findings suggest that the problem may have another origin, specifically in the bloodstream.
insights.locator: Alzheimer's disease is the most common form of dementia
insights.speaker: Rémi Lamontagne-Caron

insights.claim: In the amyloid-centric account, cognitive decline including memory loss is driven by the accumulation of two toxic proteins, amyloid plaques and tau fibres.
insights.so_what: These two proteins remain the targets of most approved and in-development dementia drugs, so any origin-shift reprices that pipeline.
insights.quote: the “rust” is characterized by the accumulation of two toxic proteins: amyloid plaques and tau fibres
insights.locator: As we age, this machinery wears out
insights.speaker: Rémi Lamontagne-Caron

insights.claim: A useful model of the aging brain treats neurons as the engine and the cerebral vascular system as pipes delivering fuel (oxygen and nutrients), so failure can start in either the delivery system or the engine itself.
insights.so_what: Framing dementia as a plumbing problem as much as an engine problem widens the addressable intervention set to vascular health, blood pressure and perfusion.
insights.locator: Imagine the brain as a car
insights.speaker: Rémi Lamontagne-Caron

insights.claim: Contrary to common belief, dementia is not just about memory, so diagnostics and outcome measures focused narrowly on memory understate the disease.
insights.so_what: Trial endpoints and screening tools built around memory alone may be missing where the disease burden actually sits.
insights.quote: Contrary to a commonly held belief, dementia isn’t just about memory.
insights.locator: Contrary to a commonly held belief
insights.speaker: Rémi Lamontagne-Caron
